Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

want verb

also would like, don’t want, feel like

classical

Ter. Ph. 950: Nōlō, volō; volō, nōlō rūrsum
Cic. Att. 12.41.1: scīre tamen volēbam ubi essēs

volō, velle, voluī

verb, irregular

want, wish, be willing

With an infinitive (scīre volēbam), an accusative and infinitive (tē venīre volō) or a bare subjunctive (quid faciam vīs?, Hor. Ep. 2.2.57). Vīn', for vīsne, offers something; the polite velim is “I’d like”.

Other words

  • nōlō, nōlle, nōluī — not want, refuse

    verb, irregular · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.11.1: festīnāre tē nōlō; Plaut. Cas. 233: Nōlō amēs.

    “I don’t want” is normally nōlō; nōlī with an infinitive is “don’t!”.

  • cupiō, cupere, cupīvī, cupītum — want eagerly, long for

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 3.7.3: vidēre tē cupiō; Cic. Fam. 14.4.1: ego vērō tē quam prīmum, mea vīta, cupiō vidēre

    Stronger than volō: the word of Cicero’s letters for longing to see someone.

  • libet, libuit (libitum est) — it pleases; I feel like (doing)

    verb, impersonal · also used · classical · Ter. And. 862: Quamobrem? — Quia libet.; Plaut. Most. 1131: ego ībō prō tē, sī tibi nōn libet; Traupman 98: quia mihi libitum est

    With a dative of the person: nōn libet, “I don’t feel like it”; ut libet, “as you like”. Comedy often spells it lubet.

Examples

  • Nōlō, volō; volō, nōlō rūrsum; cedo, cape.

    I don’t want it, I want it; I want it, then I don’t; give it here, take it.Ter. Ph. 950

  • Vīn' aquam?

    Would you like some water?Plaut. Curc. 313

  • quid faciam vīs?

    What do you want me to do?Hor. Ep. 2.2.57

  • festīnāre tē nōlō

    I don’t want you to hurry.Cic. Fam. 16.11.1

See also what do you want?, wish, I want a word with you, help.
